# Provider free tiers

**Generated by `scripts/verify_providers.py`. Do not hand-edit.**
**Last verified: 2026-08-09** (initial values researched during planning;
re-verified and regenerated on Day 1).

Free tiers change monthly — quotas move, models are withdrawn, whole tiers
disappear. Nobody maintains a current, sourced comparison of what you can
actually run an agent on for free, so this table is a small standalone
contribution as well as an input to the experiment.

Every row carries a **fetch date** and a **source URL**. A row without both is a
bug, enforced by [SPEC-001 AC-3](../specs/SPEC-001-provider-registry.md).

## What the numbers mean in practice

Raw quota numbers are misleading for agentic workloads, because a trajectory is
many calls that each resend the accumulated history. Translated into trajectories
(see [TOKEN_BUDGET.md](TOKEN_BUDGET.md) for the arithmetic):

| Model | Trajectories/day | Role in this project |
|---|---|---|
| gemini-2.5-flash-lite | ~125 | **Lane B workhorse** |
| cerebras gpt-oss-120b | ~40 | Lane B; **sets the 8K context policy for everything** |
| groq llama-3.1-8b-instant | ~33 | Lane B; also the Lane A fallback substrate |
| gemini-2.5-flash | ~31 | Lane B |
| groq llama-3.3-70b-versatile | **~6** | Model-size axis only, at disclosed low N |
| openrouter `:free` | **~6** | Breadth garnish, at disclosed low N |

---

## Things worth knowing before you plan around these

**Google cut free-tier quotas by 50–80% in December 2025.** Any blog post or
tutorial predating that is stale, often by a large factor. This is the single
most common source of wrong capacity assumptions.

**Groq's 70B is effectively unusable for agents on the free tier.** 1,000
requests/day reads as generous; 100K tokens/day is the real ceiling, and it
supports roughly six agentic trajectories. It is on the board for the model-size
axis, not as a workhorse, and every result involving it carries its N.

**Cerebras binds on two dimensions.** 1M TPD is the most generous quota here, but
the **8,192-token context ceiling** on the free tier is the constraint that
shapes the whole experiment: it is why every cell in the pooled grid runs a
capped context policy, and therefore why the compaction ablation exists. See
[EXPERIMENT_DESIGN.md §4](EXPERIMENT_DESIGN.md).

**OpenRouter's daily limit depends on account state** — 50 requests/day without
purchased credits, ~1,000/day after a one-off $10 purchase. This project uses the
no-credit tier, so 50. The `:free` model roster also shifts continuously as
providers add and pull models, which makes it unsuitable as a stable axis.

**Cerebras has no native Inspect provider.** It is reached through Inspect's
OpenAI-compatible path as `openai-api/cerebras/<model>`, requiring both
`CEREBRAS_API_KEY` and `CEREBRAS_BASE_URL`. This is why the project has no
LiteLLM dependency — see [adr/0001](adr/0001-drop-litellm.md).

**Rate limits are per organisation, not per key.** Creating more keys does not
create more quota.

## Drift detection

`scripts/verify_providers.py --check` runs nightly in CI, probes each provider,
and **exits non-zero when observed limits differ from the registry**. A silent
quota change mid-project would otherwise show up as unexplained sweep failures
days later.

When drift is detected: re-run with `--write-docs` to regenerate this file, then
re-run the budget forecast, since a quota change may invalidate the sweep plan.

---

## Lane A: local models

Lane A has no quota, so the constraints are different in kind: **VRAM residency**
and **throughput**. An 8 GB card at 4-bit tops out around 12B; a model that
spills into system RAM collapses to CPU-like speeds and becomes unusable.

Model identity here is the **digest**, never the tag. `qwen2.5:7b` six months from
now will not be the weights that produced these numbers, and a result that cannot
be reproduced is not a result. See [adr/0011](adr/0011-pin-model-digests.md).

> _Roster and measurements filled by [SPEC-010](../specs/SPEC-010-lane-a-model-gate.md) on Day 8._
